title: Review checkpoints + refactor backlog (personal notes)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for reviewing PR #3421 (kv-cache + batching fixes) and capturing follow-up refactor ideas. Not a formal doc — rough bullets, prioritization and action items to carry to the next sync.

Context / high-level: 
- PR touches: kv cache eviction, batch window heuristics, and two small api changes in request routing.
- Concern: fixes are small but invasive for stateful KV cache; want a light-touch review now and a bigger follow-up refactor (safer in 2-stage rollout).

Quick PR review checkpoints (fast pass):
- Correctness:
  - [ ] Cache keys consistent across variants (check prefix composition -> model_id + seq_len + routing-tag).
  - [ ] Eviction logic: does it correctly decrement reference counters? edge-case: early-abort requests.
  - [ ] Unit tests for race conditions (concurrency test missing).
- Behavioral/semantics:
  - [ ] Regression risk on long-lived connections (chat streaming). Add an integration smoke test.
  - [ ] Fallback behavior: if cache miss but batch present, does it still allocate KV?
- Performance safety:
  - [ ] Perf microbenchmark: p95 latency before/after with seq_len=1024, batch=8 on A100.
  - [ ] Memory: track peak GPU memory with synthetic load (kv-heavy warm starts).
- Observability:
  - [ ] Add metric: kv_eviction_reason label (capacity|ttl|manual).
  - [ ] Trace: annotate trace spans when cache hit/miss/evict.
- Code quality:
  - [ ] Inline comments explaining why we prefer max_cache_items over bytes.
  - [ ] Small functions > large monolith (split evict() into choose_candidate + release_refs).

Immediate notes from scanning PR diff:
- kv_cache.rs:evict_candidates() has a nested loop; complexity might be O(n^2) in worst case. Flag for follow-up.
- batching heuristics: magic constant 0.15 used to decide window size. Add note to parametrize and document.
- tests/unit/cache_tests.rs: good basic coverage, but no multi-threaded test. Add a stress test that spawns 64 async workers.
- missing changelog entry; ask author to add a short note for release notes.

Refactor backlog (ranked):
1) Weak-ref based KV ownership model (medium):
   - Why: current explicit ref counters are fragile across early-aborts and panics.
   - Rough plan: switch to Weak<RwLock<...>> handles stored in map; allow automatic cleanup when strong refs reach 0; keep explicit metrics for lifecycle events.
   - Risks: more GC behaviour, potential for subtle lifetime bugs. Need a small prototype branch.

2) Cache eviction algorithm rewrite (high):
   - Why: current O(n^2) scanning will blow up for large caches (seen ~7k items in staging).
   - Idea: maintain a priority queue + epoch-based lazy deletion; amortize cost.
   - Owner: probably infra+serving-runtime pair. Estimate 3-4d + benching.

3) Parametrized batching policy (low-medium):
   - Expose per-model config: min_batch, max_batch, adaptive_coefficient (replace magic constants).
   - Add UI knobs in Console later (Optimize team).

4) Integration test harness for long-tail scenarios (critical):
   - A test rig that simulates heterogeneous sequence lengths and churny streams.
   - Use existing stressing infra (see linked JIRA).

Pending follow-ups / action items (who / when):
- @Ravi: run perf microbench on PR branch and paste numbers here. (TODO: ping after review)
- @Maya: add multi-threaded stress test in tests/unit/cache_tests.rs.
- @Claire (me): write tiny RFC for Weak-ref KV ownership (1-2 pages) — target next week.
- Author: add changelog entry + note in PR description about fallback semantics.

Test checklist to gate merge:
- [ ] Unit tests pass locally + CI.
- [ ] Add stress test and ensure it runs under CI-staging (or a tagged job).
- [ ] Perf baseline captured and p95 delta < 5% for non-kv workloads.
- [ ] Observability metrics added and CI checks for new metric names.

Open questions / things to confirm:
- Does batch window heuristic interact with autoscaler (could increase bursty GPU usage)? Need to double-check with SRE.
- Are there customer-facing semantics changes (session expiry, streaming drop) that should be communicated to CS?
- Is there a runtime flag to force-disable cache for debugging? If not, consider adding one for staging.

Random notes / shorthand (keep for my follow-up):
- If we go Weak-ref route, watch out for cycles (Rc cycles) — prefer Arc + Weak.
- Consider exposing eviction events to Optimize so they can suggest model-level tuning.
- For rollout: canary to 5% dedicated capacity + metric watch (cache_hit_rate, error_rate, p95).

References & links: 
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3421
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1456 (kv cache incidents + follow-up)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (ts=1682345600)

End of scratchpad. Will extract clean checklist to PR comment if there are no major objections.
summary: Personal scratchpad for PR #3421 review: quick checklist, code smells, prioritized refactor backlog, tests and follow-ups. Draft; action items assigned to Ravi, Maya, Claire (me) and the PR author.
